title: Digesta TEI: A CTS-Addressable TEI P5 Dataset for Justinian's Digest
description:
Digesta TEI encodes all 50 books of Justinian’s Digest in TEI P5 / EpiDoc XML. Its 432 titles, 9,139 juristic fragments and 21,077 sections have stable XML identifiers and CTS-compatible references (work identifier: urn:cts:latinLit:phi2806.phi002.humanitext-lat1). Each fragment records the attributed jurist and source work in its inscriptio. The XML preserves the written forms of the names alongside 39 controlled attribution keys, and marks 346 Greek spans, 21 textual gaps and 11 editorial supplements.

The Digital Digesta project at Nagoya University digitised the four-volume Keip reprint (Goldbach, 2001) of the two-volume Mommsen–Krüger editio maior (Berlin, 1868–1870). The team checked the Humanitext OCR output against the printed text. The package includes the correction history, the attribution-key table, identifier migration tables, and a section-level crosswalk to Marton Ribary’s digest.db. The crosswalk aligns 21,033 sections by reference and records a separate comparison of opening words. Validation materials and SHA-256 checksums accompany the files.

Funded by the Future Society Creation Project (International Academia Formation Seed Fund) of the Institutes of Innovation for Future Society, Nagoya University (principal investigator: Yukiko Kawamoto).
